sentences.text: Bifidobacterium bifidum is described as an infant gut symbiont specialised in degrading host-derived glycans, and as one of the most persistent members of the human gut microbiota.

A pangenome study of 1,351 genomes reported the most extensive host-glycan degrading enzyme repertoire among human-associated bifidobacteria, with 43 percent of its conserved glycoside hydrolases devoted to these substrates.
Two phosphotransferase systems for disaccharide uptake were significantly up-regulated during growth on human milk oligosaccharides, mucin and N-acetylglucosamine.

A study of longitudinal stool samples from breastfed infants and their mothers found in co-culture that Escherichia coli supplies cysteine to Bifidobacterium bifidum, enabling cooperative degradation of 2'-fucosyllactose.
Disrupting a GH101 glycoside hydrolase gene in strain PRL2010 markedly reduced adhesion to mucin-secreting epithelial cells.
